title: Rejetto HTTP File Server RCE
rules_yaml:
title: Rejetto HFS Command Injection via Null Byte in Search Parameter
id: b06fc6b1-c4e0-4bbe-b852-eeaa3d7f2a9c
status: experimental
description: Detects exploitation of CVE-2014-6287 in Rejetto HTTP File Server using null byte injection in the search parameter to execute arbitrary commands.
references:
    - https://vk9-sec.com/hfs-code-execution-cve-2014-6287/
    - https://www.exploit-db.com/exploits/39161
    - https://github.com/Twigonometry/Cybersecurity-Notes/blob/c875b0f52df7d2c7a870e75e1f0c2679d417931d/Writeups/Hack%20the%20Box/Boxes/Optimum/10%20-%20Website.md
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1203/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/001/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/003/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1071/001/
author: Sigma Assistant
date: 2026-09-26
tags:
    - attack.execution
    - attack.t1203
    - attack.t1059.001
    - attack.t1059.003
    - attack.t1071.001
logsource:
    category: webserver
detection:
    selection:
        cs-uri-query|contains:
            - '%00{.+exec|'
            - 'search=%00'
    condition: selection
falsepositives:
    - Legitimate use of search parameter with null byte in URL
level: high

id: 5a9f0c4d-1b2e-4f5a-8c1d-7e8f9a0b1c2d
status: experimental

The attack chain involved reconnaissance using Grixba (Play Ransomware tool), network scanning with SoftPerfect NetScan and GRB_NET.exe, Active Directory enumeration with SharpHound/AdFind, credential dumping via DCSync and Veeam database access, lateral movement via RDP and PsExec, persistence through startup folder shortcuts and local account creation, and defense evasion by disabling Windows Defender and masquerading malware as legitimate security tools. The intrusion was linked to multiple ransomware groups including Play, RansomHub, and DragonForce.
